requirements.title: Run a gate of the package's commands
requirements.rationale: A model that runs the gate by hand repeats work and keeps the result in its head; one call with one verdict is the same every time.

criteria.condition: `speca <package> --gate full` is called and no passing result is recorded under the gate's key
criteria.action: run the package's `linter` command, then its `all_tests` command, each once, in the directory `--dir` names, and report the verdict `pass` when both exit with code 0
criteria.contract: exit code 0 and `ok` true; `result.gate` holds `level` "full", `verdict` "pass", `clean_env` false, `commands` with one entry per command in run order, each with `name` (`linter`, then `all_tests`), `exit_code` 0 and `seconds`, and the total `seconds`

setup: a temporary git repository with one commit, holding one package under .specs whose test_commands name two executable scripts outside the repository, each appending its own name to a file outside the repository
XDG_STATE_HOME set to an empty temporary directory
check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go (new), a table over the levels {full, task}, with the helpers run and result of cmd/speca/helpers_test.go: env, code = run('NN', '--gate', level); assert code == 0 and env.ok; g = env.result.gate; assert g.level == level and g.verdict == 'pass' and g.clean_env == false; assert names(g.commands) == ['linter', 'all_tests'] and every exit_code == 0; assert the scripts' file reads 'linter\nall_tests\n'; assert g.slowest is present for full and absent for task

criteria.condition: `speca <package> --gate task` is called and no passing result is recorded under the gate's key
criteria.action: run the same two commands in the same order and report the verdict with `level` "task"
criteria.contract: as REQ-1.1, with `level` "task"

criteria.condition: a command of the gate exits with a code other than 0
criteria.action: end the gate with the verdict `fail` and start none of the commands after it
criteria.contract: exit code 0 and `ok` true; `result.gate.verdict` is "fail"; `commands` ends with the failing command and its `exit_code`; a command after it has no entry and was not started

setup: the repository of REQ-1.1, with the linter script exiting 3
check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go: env, code = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert code == 0 and env.ok; g = env.result.gate; assert g.verdict == 'fail'; assert len(g.commands) == 1 and g.commands[0].name == 'linter' and g.commands[0].exit_code == 3; assert the all_tests script left no line in its file. A second case with linter passing and all_tests exiting 1: two entries, the second with exit_code 1

criteria.condition: a command cannot start: its program is not found, its command string has an unterminated quote, or the package's `test_commands` hold no `linter` or no `all_tests` command
criteria.action: end the gate with the verdict `not_run` and start no further command
criteria.contract: exit code 0 and `ok` true; `result.gate.verdict` is "not_run"; `result.gate.reason` names the command and says why it could not start; that command's entry, when it has one, carries no `exit_code`

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over {linter names a program that does not exist; all_tests names a program that does not exist (the linter script ran first); linter is `make 'lint` with the quote left open; tasks.json holds an empty test_commands object}: env, code = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert code == 0 and env.ok; g = env.result.gate; assert g.verdict == 'not_run'; assert g.reason contains the command's name; assert no entry of g.commands for that command has exit_code

criteria.action: start each command's program directly, with the arguments its command string holds when split on white space, a stretch inside single or double quotes kept as one argument without its quotes
criteria.contract: the program receives `|`, `&&`, `>`, `$HOME` and `*` as literal arguments, and an argument with a space when it was quoted; no shell is started

check.pseudocode: in internal/gate/command_test.go (new), a table over command strings for the function that splits one: 'make test' -> [make, test]; "go test ./... -run 'A|B'" -> [go, test, ./..., -run, A|B]; 'x "a b" c' -> [x, a b, c]; 'x  a\tb' -> [x, a, b]; 'x && y > z $HOME *' -> [x, &&, y, >, z, $HOME, *]; '' and '   ' -> an error; "x 'a" -> an error. One case through cmd/speca/gate_test.go: a script that writes its arguments one per line, named in all_tests as `<script> a|b '$HOME c' *`; assert its file holds exactly 'a|b', '$HOME c', '*'

criteria.condition: a command is still running when the time `--timeout` gives, 20 minutes when the flag is absent, has passed since it started
criteria.action: end the command and every process it started, and end the gate with the verdict `fail`
criteria.contract: exit code 0 and `ok` true; `result.gate.verdict` is "fail"; the command's entry has `timed_out` true and no `exit_code`; no process the command started is running when speca returns; nothing is recorded for reuse

setup: the repository of REQ-1.1, with an all_tests script that starts a child process sleeping 60 seconds, writes both process ids to a file outside the repository and waits
check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go: env, code = run('NN', '--gate', 'full', '--timeout', '300ms'); assert code == 0; c = last(env.result.gate.commands); assert env.result.gate.verdict == 'fail' and c.timed_out and c.exit_code is absent; assert neither recorded process id is alive; env2 = run('NN', '--gate', 'full', '--timeout', '300ms'); assert env2.result.gate.reused is absent

criteria.condition: `--gate` is given a value other than `task` or `full`
criteria.action: refuse the call before a package is read or a command is started
criteria.contract: exit code 2; `error.category` is "usage" and `error.fix_hint` names the flag `--gate` with the valid values `task` and `full`; nothing was run or written

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/main_test.go, beside the existing table of flag combinations that are refused with a usage error, the cases {--gate '', --gate all, --gate Full}: env, code = run('09', '--gate', value); assert code == 2 and env.error.category == 'usage'; assert env.error.fix_hint.flag == '--gate' and env.error.fix_hint.valid == ['task', 'full']

criteria.condition: `--gate` or `--gate-report` is combined with another form (`--validate`, `--list`, `--next`, `--task` or `--state`, `--status`, `--render`, `--migrate`, or the other of the two), is given no package, or a flag is given without its form (`--clean-env` or `--timeout` without `--gate`, `--since` without `--gate-report`), or `--timeout` is not a duration greater than zero
criteria.action: refuse the call before a package is read or a command is started
criteria.contract: exit code 2 and `error.category` "usage", with a message that names the two operations or the flag and the form it needs; nothing was run or written

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/main_test.go, the same table as REQ-1.7 with one case per combination the condition lists, among them ['09', '--gate', 'full', '--validate'], ['--gate', 'full'], ['09', '--gate', 'full', '--gate-report'], ['09', '--clean-env'], ['09', '--since', 'HEAD'], ['09', '--gate', 'full', '--timeout', '0s'], ['09', '--gate', 'full', '--timeout', 'soon']: assert code == 2 and env.error.category == 'usage' and the snapshot of the repository is as it was

requirements.title: Run the gate in a clean environment
requirements.rationale: A test that passes only on this machine's configuration fails for everyone else; the conformance pass asks for this run and should not have to build it by hand.

criteria.condition: `--clean-env` is given with `--gate`
criteria.action: run every command of the gate with `HOME` set to an empty directory created for this gate, with no global and no system git configuration read, and with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` set to `0`, every other environment variable inherited
criteria.contract: `result.gate.clean_env` is true; a command sees a `HOME` that is an empty directory, `git config --global --list` and `git config --system --list` print nothing in it, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` is `0`, and a variable set in speca's environment is still set

setup: HOME set to a temporary directory whose .gitconfig sets user.name, and a variable GATE_PROBE=1 in the environment

an all_tests script that writes, to a file outside the repository, $HOME, the listing of $HOME, $GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, $GATE_PROBE and the output of `git config --global --list` and `git config --system --list`
check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over {with --clean-env, without}: env = run('NN', '--gate', 'full', flag...); with the flag: assert env.result.gate.clean_env; assert the probe file shows a HOME other than the test's, an empty listing, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT == '0', GATE_PROBE == '1' and no git configuration line. Without it: assert clean_env == false, HOME is the test's and the global configuration lists user.name

criteria.condition: a gate run with `--clean-env` ends, with any verdict
criteria.action: remove the directory it created as `HOME`, with everything the commands wrote into it
criteria.contract: the directory a command saw as `HOME` does not exist when speca returns

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over an all_tests script that {exits 0, exits 1, runs past --timeout}, each writing $HOME to a file outside the repository and creating a file inside $HOME: run('NN', '--gate', 'full', '--clean-env', ...); assert the recorded directory does not exist

criteria.condition: a gate is run without `--clean-env`
criteria.action: run every command with speca's own environment, unchanged
criteria.contract: `result.gate.clean_env` is false; a command sees speca's `HOME` and the user's global git configuration

requirements.title: Reuse a result that passed
requirements.rationale: The baseline of one package is the merged tree of the one before, and a merged tree is often the branch tip's tree; running the suite on a tree that already passed buys nothing.

criteria.condition: a gate ends with the verdict `pass` in a git work tree
criteria.action: record the result outside the repository, under `agent-fox/speca` in the user's state directory (`$XDG_STATE_HOME`, else `~/.local/state`), keyed by the tree id of the working tree with tracked and untracked files included and ignored files left out, the level, the exact `linter` and `all_tests` command strings, and whether the environment was clean
criteria.contract: after the call a record exists under the state directory and no file is new under `--dir`; a later call with the same key is answered from it

criteria.condition: a gate is called and a passing result is recorded under its key
criteria.action: start no command and answer with the recorded pass
criteria.contract: exit code 0; `result.gate.verdict` is "pass"; `reused` holds `commit` (the commit that was checked out at the recorded run), `at` (the time of that run, RFC 3339) and `seconds` (its total); `commands` is empty and `seconds` is 0; for a full gate `slowest` is the recorded run's

setup: the repository of REQ-1.1, whose scripts count their runs in a file outside the repository
check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go: first = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert first.result.gate.reused is absent and the scripts ran once; assert a file exists under $XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-fox/speca and the snapshot of the repository is as it was; second = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); g = second.result.gate; assert g.verdict == 'pass' and g.reused.commit == rev-parse(HEAD) and g.reused.at parses as RFC 3339 and g.reused.seconds == first.result.gate.seconds; assert g.commands == [] and g.seconds == 0 and g.slowest == first.result.gate.slowest; assert the scripts still ran once

criteria.action: for any gate whose key differs from every recorded pass in one part (the content of a tracked file, an untracked file that is not ignored, the level, a command string, or the clean environment), run the commands
criteria.contract: `result.gate.reused` is absent and both commands were started

setup: the repository of REQ-3.2 after one passing `--gate full`, with a .gitignore that ignores *.log
check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table of one change each, the gate run after it and the expected answer: {edit a tracked file -> ran; add an untracked file notes.txt -> ran; call --gate task -> ran; change the all_tests string in tasks.json by one argument -> ran; add --clean-env -> ran; add an ignored file x.log -> reused; commit the uncommitted change that the last pass covered -> reused, with reused.commit the commit before it; merge a branch with --no-ff whose tip's tree passed, the base not having moved -> reused}: assert reused is present exactly where the table says, and the scripts' run count rose exactly where it says ran

criteria.action: for any two working trees that hold the same files with the same content, use one key whatever commit is checked out and whatever the ignored files hold
criteria.contract: a gate on the second tree is answered with `reused` naming the commit of the first run

criteria.condition: a gate ends with the verdict `fail` or `not_run`
criteria.action: record nothing that a later gate could reuse
criteria.contract: the next call with the same key starts the commands again and its `result.gate.reused` is absent

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over {all_tests exits 1, linter names a missing program}: a = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); b = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert a.result.gate.verdict == b.result.gate.verdict and b.result.gate.reused is absent; for the failing script assert it ran twice

criteria.action: work out the tree id without changing the repository: the user's index, the staged changes, the working tree and every file under `.git` stay as they were
criteria.contract: with staged, unstaged and untracked changes present, every file under `--dir`, `.git` and its index and object store included, has the same content, size and mode after a gate as before it, and `git status --porcelain` prints the same

setup: the repository of REQ-1.1 with one staged edit, one unstaged edit and one untracked file
check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, with the helper snapshot of cmd/speca/helpers_test.go: before = snapshot(root); status = git('status', '--porcelain'); run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert snapshot(root) == before; assert git('status', '--porcelain') == status; assert git('diff', '--cached', '--name-only') still names the staged file alone

criteria.condition: `--dir` is not inside a git work tree, or `git` is not installed
criteria.action: run the gate and answer with its verdict, recording nothing
criteria.contract: exit code 0; `result.gate.verdict` is what the commands returned; `warnings` holds one `gate_not_recorded` entry whose message says there is no tree id to record the result under; a second call starts the commands again

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over {a directory with .specs and no .git, a repository with PATH holding no git}: a = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert a.exit_code == 0 and a.result.gate.verdict == 'pass'; assert codes(a.warnings) == ['gate_not_recorded']; b = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert b.result.gate.reused is absent and the scripts ran twice

criteria.condition: the state directory cannot be created or written, or a recorded result under the gate's key cannot be parsed
criteria.action: run the gate and answer with its verdict
criteria.contract: exit code 0; `result.gate.verdict` is what the commands returned; where the directory cannot be written, `warnings` holds one `gate_not_recorded` entry naming the path and each command's `log` is absent; where a record cannot be parsed, it counts as no record, and the pass replaces it

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, two cases. XDG_STATE_HOME names a regular file: a = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert a.exit_code == 0 and a.result.gate.verdict == 'pass' and codes(a.warnings) == ['gate_not_recorded'] and the warning's message contains the path; assert no command entry has log. A recorded pass overwritten with 'not json': b = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert b.result.gate.reused is absent and the scripts ran; c = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); assert c.result.gate.reused is present

requirements.title: Keep a command's output in a log and its failure in the verdict
requirements.rationale: A test suite's output is thousands of lines the model does not need; the forty that explain a failure are the ones it does.

criteria.condition: a command of the gate runs
criteria.action: write everything the command prints to stdout and stderr to one log file of its own under the state directory, and name the file in the command's `log`
criteria.contract: `log` is an absolute path that is not under `--dir`; the file holds the command's complete output

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go: with a linter script printing 'out-1' to stdout and 'err-1' to stderr and an all_tests script printing 3000 numbered lines: env = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); for each c of env.result.gate.commands: assert c.log is absolute and not under root and under $XDG_STATE_HOME; assert read(commands[0].log) contains 'out-1' and 'err-1'; assert read(commands[1].log) holds all 3000 lines in order; assert the two paths differ

criteria.condition: a command exits with a code other than 0 or is ended by the timeout
criteria.action: put the last 40 lines of the command's output in its `tail`
criteria.contract: `tail` holds the last 40 lines of the output in order, all of them when the output has fewer, and is an empty string when the command printed nothing; a command that exited with 0 has no `tail`

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over a failing all_tests script that prints {0, 1, 40, 41, 500} numbered lines, and one that prints 41 lines with no newline after the last: env = run('NN', '--gate', 'full'); c = last(env.result.gate.commands); assert lines(c.tail) == the last min(n, 40) lines printed, in order; assert the passing linter's entry has no tail

criteria.action: keep everything a command prints off its own stdout
criteria.contract: speca's stdout is exactly one JSON object, whatever the commands print and however much

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go: with a linter script that prints '{"ok":false}' and an all_tests script that prints 5 MB: out = the bytes speca wrote to stdout for ['NN', '--gate', 'full']; assert json.decode(out) succeeds with nothing left over; assert out does not contain the scripts' text

requirements.title: Measure what a gate costs
requirements.rationale: The suite of the measured run grew from ten seconds to nearly three minutes and nobody noticed, because nothing wrote a duration down.

criteria.action: record the wall-clock seconds each command of a gate ran, and report the gate's total as their sum
criteria.contract: each `commands[i].seconds` is a number of seconds, zero or more, to the millisecond; `result.gate.seconds` equals their sum

setup: the gate runner's clock replaced by one that advances 1.5 s during the first command and 2.25 s during the second
check.pseudocode: in internal/gate/run_test.go (new): r = run the gate with two commands that exit 0; assert r.commands[0].seconds == 1.5 and r.commands[1].seconds == 2.25 and r.seconds == 3.75

criteria.condition: the `all_tests` command of a full gate has run and its output holds Go's per-package result lines
criteria.action: report the five packages with the most seconds, slowest first, as `slowest`
criteria.contract: `slowest` holds at most five entries `{unit, seconds}`, ordered by seconds descending, entries with equal seconds in output order; a line `ok <package> <n>s` or `FAIL <package> <n>s` is a unit, with or without text after the duration; a line with `(cached)` or `[no test files]` is not

check.pseudocode: in internal/gate/units_test.go (new), a table over outputs for the function that reads the units: {no line -> []; three ok lines -> three entries, slowest first; seven lines, one of them FAIL -> the five slowest, the FAIL line among them when its seconds place it; 'ok  \tpkg/a\t(cached)' and '?   \tpkg/b\t[no test files]' -> not units; 'ok  \tpkg/c\t0.512s\tcoverage: 81.0% of statements' -> {pkg/c, 0.512}; two lines of 1.000s -> output order; pytest and Jest output -> []}

criteria.condition: the `all_tests` command of a full gate has run and its output holds no line speca recognises
criteria.action: report an empty list of slowest units
criteria.contract: `result.gate.slowest` is present and is `[]`

criteria.condition: a task gate has run
criteria.action: report no list of slowest units
criteria.contract: `result.gate.slowest` is absent

requirements.title: Sum a package's gate runs for the merge commit
requirements.rationale: The merge commit and the report must say what the gates cost from something that was measured, not from what a model remembers.

criteria.condition: `speca <package> --gate-report --since <commit>` is called
criteria.action: count the gate runs recorded for this package that ended in `pass` or `fail`, reused ones included, whose checked-out commit is `<commit>` or a descendant of it reachable from `HEAD` or, while a merge is uncommitted, from `MERGE_HEAD`
criteria.contract: exit code 0; `result.gate_report` holds `since` (the full id of the commit) and, under `full` and under `task`, `runs`, `seconds` (the sum of the runs' own seconds, a reused run adding 0) and `reused`; a run of another package, a `not_run` gate and a run at a commit outside that range are not counted

setup: a repository with two packages and the commits B (base), then F1, F2 and F3 on a branch, and a commit X on another branch

gates run through speca itself: package one full at B, task at F1, task again at F1 (reused), full failing at F2, full passing at F3, which commits the fix; package two full at B; package one full at X; package one full with a missing linter program at F3
check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_report_test.go (new): on F3: env = run('<one>', '--gate-report', '--since', B); r = env.result.gate_report; assert env.exit_code == 0 and r.since == B; assert r.full.runs == 3 and r.full.reused == 0; assert r.task.runs == 2 and r.task.reused == 1; assert r.full.seconds == the sum of the three full runs' seconds as their verdicts reported them. Then on the base, after `git merge --no-ff --no-commit <branch>` and one more `--gate full`: assert the report counts 4 full runs and full.reused == 1, the merged tree being F3's

criteria.action: report the duration of the earliest full run counted as `baseline_full_seconds`, that of the latest as `last_full_seconds`, a reused run's duration being that of the run it came from, and the slowest units of the latest full run as `slowest`
criteria.contract: `baseline_full_seconds` and `last_full_seconds` are numbers of seconds; `slowest` is the list the latest full run's verdict held, the recorded run's list when that run was reused

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_report_test.go, in the scenario of the test above with an all_tests script that prints two Go result lines: assert r.baseline_full_seconds == the seconds of the full gate at B; assert r.last_full_seconds == the seconds of the passing full gate at F3; after the reused gate on the merged tree: assert r.last_full_seconds is still that number and not 0, and r.slowest == the two units, slowest first

criteria.condition: no recorded run counts: the state directory holds no run of this package in the range, or no run log at all, or only lines that cannot be parsed
criteria.action: report a count of zero for every number
criteria.contract: exit code 0; `full` and `task` each hold `runs` 0, `seconds` 0 and `reused` 0; `baseline_full_seconds` and `last_full_seconds` are absent; `slowest` is `[]`

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_report_test.go, a table over {an empty state directory, a run log holding one run of another package, a run log holding 'not json' and one run of this package (that run is counted, the line skipped)}: env = run('<one>', '--gate-report', '--since', 'HEAD'); assert env.exit_code == 0; for the first two: assert every count is 0, both durations are absent and slowest == []; for the third: assert full.runs == 1

criteria.condition: `speca <package> --gate-report` is called without `--since`
criteria.action: take as the commit the merge base of `HEAD` and the base branch, which is the branch `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` names, else `main`
criteria.contract: `result.gate_report.since` is the full id of that merge base, and the runs are counted from it

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_report_test.go, a table over {a clone whose origin/HEAD names a branch trunk, a repository with no remote and a branch main}: on a feature branch two commits ahead: env = run('<one>', '--gate-report'); assert env.result.gate_report.since == git('merge-base', 'HEAD', base)

criteria.condition: `--since` names no commit of the repository, or `--since` is absent and neither `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` nor a branch `main` exists, or `--dir` is not inside a git work tree
criteria.action: refuse the call
criteria.contract: exit code 2 and `error.category` "usage"; the message names the value that is no commit, or says to give `--since <commit>`, or says the directory is not a git work tree; there is no `result`

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_report_test.go, a table over {--since nosuchref; no --since in a repository whose only branch is work; a directory with .specs and no .git}: env, code = run('<one>', '--gate-report', ...); assert code == 2 and env.error.category == 'usage' and env.result is absent; assert env.error.message contains 'nosuchref', '--since' or 'git' as the case has it

requirements.title: Leave the repository alone and describe the two forms
requirements.rationale: A gate is a measurement, not a task move, and an agent learns a command from its own description.

criteria.action: for any lifecycle status of the package (draft, active, sealed, superseded, archived), run `--gate` and `--gate-report` and leave every file and directory under `--dir` as it was
criteria.contract: the gate answers with a verdict and the report with its counts in every status; no file under `--dir`, the package's `progress.json` and `spec.md` and the `.git` directory included, is created, changed or removed

setup: a git repository with one package per status, the superseded and archived ones under .specs/archive and named by their path, each with passing scripts that write outside the repository
check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/gate_test.go, a table over the five statuses, with the helpers packageWith and snapshot of cmd/speca/helpers_test.go: before = snapshot(root); a = run(ref, '--gate', 'full'); b = run(ref, '--gate', 'task'); c = run(ref, '--gate-report', '--since', 'HEAD'); assert a.result.gate.verdict == 'pass' and b.result.gate.verdict == 'pass' and c.result.gate_report.full.runs == 1; assert snapshot(root) == before

criteria.condition: `speca --schema` is called
criteria.action: describe the flags `--gate` with its two values, `--clean-env`, `--timeout`, `--gate-report` and `--since`, and the result fields `gate` and `gate_report` with every field of each
criteria.contract: the JSON document's `flags` holds the five flags, `gate` with the enumeration `task`, `full`; its `result` schema holds `gate` and `gate_report` with a description for every field

check.pseudocode: extends TestSchema_DescribesTheFormsFlagsAndResult in cmd/speca/schema_test.go: assert flags has gate, clean-env, timeout, gate-report and since; assert flags.gate.enum == ['task', 'full']; assert result.properties.result has gate and gate_report, and that every property under each has a description. TestSchema_MatchesTheGoldenFile in the same file compares the document with cmd/speca/testdata/schema.golden.json, which is written again

criteria.action: say in the envelope's `summary` the level, the verdict and the seconds of a gate, or the commit a reused pass came from, and for the report the runs it counted
criteria.contract: `speca: <directory> <level> gate <verdict> in <n>s` for a gate that ran; `speca: <directory> <level> gate pass, reused from <short commit>` for a reused one; `speca: <directory> <level> gate not_run: <reason>` for one that could not start; `speca: <directory> gate report: <n> full, <m> task, <k> reused` for the report

check.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/result_test.go, beside the existing tests of Result.Summary, a table over results holding a gate {full pass 42.5 s, task fail 3 s, full pass reused from abc1234, full not_run with a reason} and a gate report {3 full, 9 task, 2 reused}: assert r.Summary() equals the sentence the contract gives for each

execution_paths.title: An implementer gates a tree, gates it again unchanged, and reads the report

steps.action: runs `speca <package> --gate full` on the unchanged base branch, the baseline
asks git for the tree id of the working tree through a temporary index and finds no recorded pass under the key
runs `linter`, then `all_tests`, writing each command's output to its log and timing it
records the pass under the key and the run in the package's run log
commits a change on a branch and runs `speca <package> --gate task`, runs `--gate full` on the branch tip, then merges the branch with `--no-ff --no-commit` and runs `--gate full` on the merged tree
runs the commands for the changed tree, and for the merged tree answers `pass` with `reused`, because its tree is the branch tip's and that tree passed a full gate
runs `speca <package> --gate-report --since <baseline commit>` and copies the counts into the merge commit

real_components: the gate's commands as real processes
setup: a temporary git repository with a branch main and one package whose test_commands name two executable scripts that count their runs outside the repository, the all_tests script printing two Go result lines
XDG_STATE_HOME set to an empty temporary directory
end_state: the scripts ran for the baseline, for the task gate and for the full gate on the branch tip, and not for the merged tree
the gate on the merged tree answers `pass` with `reused.commit` the branch tip
the report counts three full runs with one reused and one task run, and holds the baseline's duration and two slowest units
the repository holds no file the gates wrote
smoke.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/e2e_test.go, beside TestAnAgentFollowsNextFromTheReportToTheFinishedTask: base = rev-parse(main); run(pkg, '--gate', 'full'); switch -c feature; write and commit a file; run(pkg, '--gate', 'task'); full = run(pkg, '--gate', 'full'); tip = rev-parse(HEAD); switch main; merge --no-ff --no-commit feature; merged = run(pkg, '--gate', 'full'); assert merged.result.gate.reused.commit == tip and the run count did not rise; rep = run(pkg, '--gate-report', '--since', base).result.gate_report; assert rep.full.runs == 3 and rep.full.reused == 1 and rep.task.runs == 1 and len(rep.slowest) == 2 and rep.baseline_full_seconds is present; assert git('status', '--porcelain') lists only the merge's own changes

execution_paths.title: A conformance pass runs the gate in a clean environment and reads the failure from the verdict

steps.action: runs `speca <package> --gate full --clean-env` on a branch whose tests pass on this machine
creates an empty directory, runs the commands with it as `HOME`, with no global or system git configuration and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`
sees `all_tests` exit non-zero, stops, puts the last 40 lines of its output in the verdict and removes the directory
records the run in the run log and no pass to reuse
reads the failure from `tail`, without opening the log, and runs the same call again after the fix

real_components: the gate's commands as real processes
setup: a temporary git repository with one package whose all_tests script exits 0 when `git config --global user.name` prints a name and otherwise prints 60 lines and exits 1
HOME set to a temporary directory whose .gitconfig sets user.name
end_state: the gate with `--clean-env` on the same tree is not reused, answers `fail`, and its `tail` holds the last 40 of the 60 lines
a second gate with `--clean-env` runs the commands again
smoke.pseudocode: in cmd/speca/e2e_test.go: a = run(pkg, '--gate', 'full'); assert a.result.gate.verdict == 'pass'; b = run(pkg, '--gate', 'full', '--clean-env'); g = b.result.gate; assert g.reused is absent and g.verdict == 'fail' and g.clean_env; assert lines(last(g.commands).tail) == lines 21 to 60; c = run(pkg, '--gate', 'full', '--clean-env'); assert c.result.gate.reused is absent; assert the HOME the script recorded does not exist
